front: Black bear or grizzly: name the 4 shape clues.
back: Shoulder hump, face profile, ears, front claws. Use at least 3 (85%).

front: Does a black bear have a shoulder hump?
back: No. Its rump is the high point of the back (90%). A grizzly's hump is the high point.

front: Black bear face profile?
back: Straight from forehead to nose. A grizzly's is dished (90%).

front: Black bear ears vs grizzly ears?
back: Black bear: taller, more pointed. Grizzly: short and round (85%).

front: Can you ID a black bear by colour?
back: No. Interior black bears are often brown, cinnamon or blond (90%). Shape, not colour.

front: Is there a grizzly season in BC?
back: No open season anywhere in BC (98%).

front: White (Kermode) or blue (Glacier) black bear: legal?
back: Never. Item 15, page 11 (99%).

front: Which bears are never legal under item 14?
back: A black bear under 2 years old, and any bear in its company (99%).

front: What does the synopsis notice ask bear hunters to select?
back: An adult male bear. "Be patient. Don't shoot the moment you see a bear!" (98%)

front: Adult male black bear weight in BC?
back: 80 to 300 kg (90%, BC account).

front: Adult female black bear weight in BC?
Black bear shoulder height, adult males?
back: 60 to 90 cm, about waist high (90%).

front: How many races of black bear in BC?
back: 6, more than anywhere in Canada (90%).

front: Which race lives around Heffley Creek and the Okanagan?
back: U. a. cinnamomum: interior, brown phase common (90%).

front: Which race lives in the Fraser Valley?
back: U. a. altifrontalis: south coast, mostly black (90%).

front: Often quoted number of black bears in BC?
back: 120,000 to 160,000, about a quarter of Canada's (BC account). Data thin (70%).

front: MU 3-27 black bear success, 2020 to 2024?
back: About 1 hunter in 4; about 28 hunter days per bear (90%, computed).

front: Black bear claw length?
back: Rarely over about 3.8 cm (1.5 in); short and curved for climbing (85%).

front: What does plantigrade mean?
back: Flat footed: the whole sole touches the ground, like ours (90%).

front: How fast can a lean black bear run?
back: Over 48 km/h (30 mph) (70%). You cannot outrun one.

front: Where do you aim on a broadside black bear?
back: Halfway up, tight behind the shoulder, near leg forward, through both lungs (85%).

front: Bear vital zone size?
back: About a 20 cm (8 in) circle behind the shoulder (85%).

front: How thick are a bear's fat and hair?
back: Fat 2.5 to 5 cm, hair 8 to 10 cm. It looks bigger than it is (70%).

front: Why are head and shoulder shots on bears a bad idea?
back: Dense, sloped skull deflects bullets; heavy shoulder bone (85%).

front: How many stomachs does a bear have?
back: One simple stomach and a short gut. It digests fibre poorly (90%).

front: About how much of a black bear's diet is plants?
back: About 80% (75%, WildSafeBC).

front: How much heavier is a bear in fall?
back: About 20% heavier than after the den (85%, Alaska).

front: Den heart rate?
back: About 50 to 55 a minute drops to about 10 to 14 (80 to 90%).

front: Den metabolism?
back: About 25% of normal, with body temperature only 3 to 6°C lower (80%).

front: Weight lost in the den?
back: Up to a quarter of body weight (90%). WildSafeBC says about 30% (75%).

front: What does a denned bear not do for months?
back: Eat, drink, urinate or defecate (90%).

front: When does a sow first breed, and how often?
back: Usually about age 4, then every 2 to 3 years (90%).

front: Typical wild lifespan?
back: 15 to 20 years typical; over 30 possible (75%, WildSafeBC).

front: Rank a bear's senses.
back: Nose first, ears second, eyes third (70%).

front: How much bigger is a bear's nose lining than ours?
back: About 100 times the area (70%, North American Bear Center).

front: How far can a bear smell food?
back: Over 1 km (70%, WildSafeBC).

front: Bear hearing vs ours?
back: Over twice as sensitive, with a higher range (70%).

front: Do bears see colour?
back: Yes, and sharp up close; distance vision untested (70%).

front: Morning vs evening thermals?
back: Morning: air drifts uphill. Evening: downhill (80%).

front: When do you move on a feeding bear?
back: When its head is down and it feeds noisily. Freeze when it looks up (Tip).

front: A bear stands on its hind legs. Why?
back: Usually to see and smell better, not to charge (Tip).

front: Signs of an agitated, defensive bear?
back: Jaw popping, woofing, moaning, stomping, bluff charge (75%).

front: Defensive vs predatory bear?
back: Defensive: noisy, fast, surprised. Predatory: quiet, stalks, keeps coming: spray and fight back (75%).

front: Fatal black bear attacks in BC?
back: Fewer than one every 3 years on average (75%, WildSafeBC).

front: Black bear social groups?
back: Mostly solitary: sow with cubs, and the brief mating pair (90%).

front: How long do cubs stay with the sow?
back: Their first year and first winter; on their own by the middle or end of their 2nd spring (90%).

front: Boar home range vs sow?
back: Boar 25 to 150 km2; sow 5 to 25 km2 (90%).

front: Boar behaviours to watch for?
back: Rubbing trees, breaking saplings, chasing and dominating other bears (65%).

front: Bears near people: when do they feed?
back: More at night (75%).

front: At what distance do you use bear spray?
back: About 5 to 10 m (75%, WildSafeBC).

front: How often did spray stop black bears in the Alaska study?
back: About 90% (92% brown bears); 98% of spray carriers uninjured (80%).

front: Where do you carry bear spray?
back: On the chest or hip, never in the pack (75%).

front: When do black bears mate?
back: Early June to mid July (90%).

front: What is delayed implantation?
back: The embryo waits and implants only in October or November, if the sow is fat enough (75 to 90%).

front: When and how big are cubs born?
back: January or February in the den, about 400 g (90%).

front: Cub weight leaving the den?
back: About 2 to 5 kg (75 to 90%).

front: Den exit near the Okanagan (Gaines 2003)?
back: Males 4 April to 7 May; females 4 April to 22 May (80%).

front: Den entry near the Okanagan (Gaines 2003)?
back: Females 15 Oct to 19 Nov; males 22 Oct to 19 Nov (80%).

front: Who dens first and comes out last?
back: Sows, especially with cubs. Big males den last (80%).

front: How long do interior bears den?
back: Probably 5 to 7 months; 3 to 5 on the south coast (90%).

front: What is hyperphagia?
back: The late summer and fall feeding frenzy: up to 20,000 calories a day (70%).

front: Spring bear foods?
back: Grasses, sedges, horsetail, skunk cabbage, south slopes, avalanche chutes, burns; newborn fawns and calves (90%).

front: Fall bear foods?
back: Berries and spawning fish; fruit and apples (90%).

front: Region 3 black bear seasons, most MUs?
back: 1 April to 30 June and 1 September to 30 November; bag 2 (99%, page 34).

front: Region 3, MU 3-46 fall bear opener?
back: 20 September (99%, page 34).

front: Region 2 black bear seasons?
back: 1 Apr to 15 June; 10 Sept to 30 Nov; bow only 1 to 9 Sept (99%, page 28).

front: Region 8 August bear season?
back: 1 to 31 Aug, private land only, with the owner's permission (99%, page 68).

front: Bear bag limit?
back: 2 per licence year, 1 April to 31 March (99%).

front: When are black bears most active?
back: Mainly by day, with dawn and dusk peaks; more at night near people (65 to 75%).

front: Legal hours for bear?
back: 1 hour before sunrise to 1 hour after sunset; no lights or infrared optics (99%).

front: Does the moon change bear movement?
back: No good bear data found: VERIFY. Do not plan around it.

front: How long can a fall bear forage in a day?
back: Up to about 20 hours (65%).

front: Where are black bears absent?
back: Most alpine, grassland and heavily settled land (90%).

front: Which cutblocks feed bears?
back: About 5 to 20 years old (Hunt Map tip). Dense second growth makes little bear food (90%).

front: Why are coastal bear densities higher?
back: Spawning salmon (90%).

front: Haida Gwaii stream study: salmon moved by bears?
back: About 3,700 salmon (10,000 kg) along 800 m in a season; about half of each eaten (75%).

front: Spring elevation of bears?
back: Low: south slopes, valley bottoms, riparian strips (85%).

front: Fall elevation of bears?
back: Follows berries upslope, then back down to fruit and fish (70%).

front: No hunting within how far of a dwelling or occupied farm building?
Black bear front and hind track sizes?
back: Front about 11 x 10 cm; hind about 18 x 9 cm, like a wide human foot (65%).

front: Straight edge track test?
back: Edge across the top of the front pad cuts the toes: black bear. Toes above the line: grizzly (80%).

front: Claw marks ahead of toe pads: black vs grizzly?
back: Black 2.5 to 6.4 cm (1 to 2.5 in); grizzly 5 to 11.4 cm (2 to 4.5 in) (80%).

front: 6 kinds of bear sign?
back: Scat, torn logs, rub trees, claw marks, flipped rocks, worn trails (85 to 90%).

front: What do bears do on old trails?
back: Step in the same footprints, year after year (90%).

front: What does fresh fall bear scat usually hold?
back: Berries and seeds; tells you what is ripe now (Tip).

front: Raked mound of debris, birds, rot smell?
back: Likely a bear cache. Back away; a bear may be bedded close (85%).

front: Can you hunt bears over bait or a carcass?
back: No. Item 21, page 11 and note 6, page 13 (99%).

front: Electronic calls for bear?
back: No. Only wolf, coyote, cougar, lynx, bobcat and Schedule C birds (99%, page 12).

front: Mouth or hand calls for bear?
back: Allowed, my reading: only recorded or electronic calls are banned (95%).

front: Unleashed dogs for black bear?
back: Allowed, page 12 (99%).

front: Can you use a rimfire for black bear?
back: No (99%, page 13).

front: Shotgun rule for black bear?
back: 20 gauge or larger, No. 1 Buck or larger (99%, page 13).

front: Synopsis: young bear clues?
back: All legs, looks over its shoulder, pointed head, big looking ears close together, thin neck (98%).

front: Synopsis: large adult male clues?
back: Stocky legs, belly near the ground, slow, round head, small looking ears, thick neck (98%).

front: Judge a bear in 4 steps?
back: Species, cubs, sex and size, then the shot (Tip).

front: How long to watch a lone bear for cubs?
back: At least 5 minutes (Tip, quick lesson).

front: Partner roles on a bear?
back: One glasses and watches for cubs; one stalks and shoots (Tip).

front: First thing at a dead bear?
back: Cancel the species licence before handling it (99%, item 1).

front: Must you take bear meat?
back: Yes. The edible portions rule applies to black bear (99%).

front: Gall bladder rule?
back: Remove and leave it at the kill site, or dispose of the gut pile with it within 48 hours (99%).

front: Bear paws?
back: Keep your own for personal use; never sell or trade them (99%).

front: Evidence of sex for black bear?
back: No rule on page 15 (99%).

front: Taking a bear hide out of Canada?
back: CITES export permit (99%, page 16).

front: Wait after a lung hit?
back: About 30 minutes (70 to 85%).

front: Why skin a bear right away?
back: Fat and hide hold heat: meat spoils and hair slips (85%).

front: Hide storage rule?
back: Game bag or burlap, never plastic (85%).

front: Salt for a black bear hide?
back: About 4.5 to 7 kg (10 to 15 lb), non iodized (85%).

front: Which parts of the face need turning or splitting?
back: Ears turned, lips and eyelids split, nose trimmed to about 2.5 cm (85%).

front: Bear skull score?
back: Length plus width of the cleaned skull, after 60 days drying (75%).

front: Safe internal temperature for bear meat?
back: 71°C (160°F), checked with a thermometer (85%).

front: Does freezing kill Trichinella in bear?
back: No. Trichinella nativa survives freezing for months or years (85%).

front: BC bear meat outbreak, 2005?
back: Victoria: frozen black bear meat; 26 probable cases among 42 eaters (75%).

front: Which bear fat makes good lard?
back: Fall fat from a berry fed bear; fish fed fat tastes fishy (Tip).
